name: Up, Up and Away
description: How a 1938 comic book with a man lifting a car started a genre that now dominates cinema, from Superman and Batman to Spider-Man and manga heroes.

checkpoints.name: The golden age
checkpoints.note: A new company, a strong man from another planet and a bat-suited detective launched comic books as a mass medium, and soon heroes were fighting the Second World War.

checkpoints.name: The backlash
checkpoints.note: A psychiatrist's book and a Senate hearing blamed comics for crime among the young, and publishers adopted a strict code that kept the stories tame.

checkpoints.name: The Marvel revolution
checkpoints.note: Stan Lee and Jack Kirby gave heroes everyday troubles and hit a nerve. Meanwhile Japan produced its own heroes and a Holocaust memoir showed what comics could say.

checkpoints.name: Grown-up comics
checkpoints.note: Darker, more thoughtful comics such as Watchmen and The Dark Knight Returns won adult readers, while manga reached new audiences around the world.
